content: The test image shows a mango leaf with irregular dark brown/black patches scattered across the leaf surface. Now let me view reference images to compare.

Analyzing the test image and Anthracnose reference:

**Test image observations:**
- Flat, green mango leaf
- Multiple irregular dark brown/black patches scattered across the leaf blade
- Patches appear angular, distributed throughout the leaf (not just margins)
- No powdery white coating, no galls, no curling/crumpling

**Comparison:**
- **Anthracnose** reference shows yellowed/curled leaves with tan-brown margin lesions and edge damage — doesn't match the test image's green leaf with angular black patches spread across the blade
- **Bacterial Canker** description: "Raised black angular spots on leaves with greasy margins and chlorotic halos" — the dark angular patches distributed across a green leaf match this well
- **Sooty Mould** would show a more uniform black coating rather than distinct patches
- Other classes (Powdery Mildew, Gall Midge, Cutting Weevil, Die_Back) don't match the morphology

The dark, angular black spots distributed across the green leaf surface most closely align with Bacterial Canker symptoms rather than Anthracnose (which shows lighter tan-brown margin lesions on yellowing leaves).
